dominant_language_across_sites: isiXhosa (78.6-94% at every death site; English 2.7-9.3%)
warning_language_evidence: No source found stating the language of the June 2025 warnings. Daily Dispatch (2026-06-23): 'All warnings were shared with the National Disaster Management Centre (NDMC) and then disseminated through social media' and via 'interviews, live radio and television' - https://www.dailydispatch.co.za/news/2026-06-23-saws-draws-global-praise-for-life-saving-mthatha-flood-warnings/ . Daily Maverick (2025-06-19): 'The weather warnings are also sent through disaster management WhatsApp groups, which are also used to send information to communities in rural areas.' and 'these systems often break down, particularly in reaching the people who need the warnings most.' - https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2025-06-19-eaastern-cape-floods-why-sas-disaster-management-and-legislation-failed/ . Related (not Mthatha): The Conversation (Mokhele & Mvanyashe, 16 Jun 2026) on isiXhosa-speaking Walmer Airport Valley, Gqeberha: disaster warnings 'are still sent out almost entirely in English and Afrikaans' - https://theconversation.com/language-matters-for-disaster-warnings-this-community-didnt-get-useful-flood-alerts-284723

death_sites.geo_level: metropolitan municipality (Nelson Mandela Bay) - Chatty not found as a 2011 census place

dominant_language_across_sites: Mixed: KwaNobuhle (4 deaths) isiXhosa 94%; Kariega/Kamesh Afrikaans 69-96%; Kabega Park/Walmer suburbs English plurality. isiXhosa- or Afrikaans-majority places account for 8 of 10 NMB deaths.
warning_language_evidence: Event-specific: none found. Directly relevant study of Walmer Airport Valley (Gqebera), Gqeberha - The Conversation (Mokhele & Mvanyashe, 16 Jun 2026): disaster warnings are 'sent out almost entirely in English and Afrikaans'; of 270 residents surveyed, 210 said 'they had never received an early warning message'; 258 owned mobile phones but only 90 'had ever received a warning through their device'; argues for plain isiXhosa over a 'jargon-filled English message'. https://theconversation.com/language-matters-for-disaster-warnings-this-community-didnt-get-useful-flood-alerts-284723 . SAWS had issued 'an Orange level 6 warning for disruptive rain' (Algoa FM).
notes: DM 9 Jun: 10 NMB deaths (KwaNobuhle 4, Kamesh 1, Kabega Park 1, Chatty 1, Walmer 1, Kariega 2, + Swartkops drowning - sums to 11 as listed; DM headline says 10). Algoa FM earlier: Kariega 4, Kabega Park & Walmer 2. Buffalo City: 1 pedestrian fatally struck in West Bank; 20-year-old missing near Dawn (SAnews). Wikipedia: 11 in EC.
